slides.title: Geometric Domains: The 5 Gs
slides.notes: Open by framing the chapter as a domain design lecture. The names are memorable, but the useful habit is to ask what structure a domain gives to a model: which transformations are harmless, where locality lives, and what coordinate choices should disappear from the computation.

slides.title: The Domain Contract
slides.notes: Use this slide as the unifying grammar for the rest of the lecture. A geometric model is not chosen by layer names first. It starts by naming the domain, the signal space, the transformation family, and the desired response of the output when the input is transformed.

slides.title: Sets And Graphs Start With Permutations
slides.notes: Emphasize the difference between forgetting order and respecting relabeling. For a set readout, reordering the rows should change nothing. For a graph node update, the output should relabel in exactly the same way, because the node identities move with the adjacency matrix.

slides.title: Local Graph Maps Are Shared Neighborhood Tests
slides.notes: The key move is to apply the same local rule at every node while feeding that rule an unordered multiset of neighbor features. This is why graph neural layers combine locality with permutation equivariance, and why the expressive power of the neighborhood function matters.

slides.title: Grids Add Ordered Neighbors
slides.notes: Contrast the ring grid with the previous graph. The nodes still form a graph, but each node has a left and right neighbor, so the local rule can use ordered offsets. Weight sharing across shifts gives a circulant matrix, and commutation with shift is the algebraic signature of convolution.

slides.title: Fourier Modes Are The Coordinates Of Shift Symmetry
slides.notes: Present the Fourier transform as a consequence of symmetry rather than a lookup table. Every circulant operator commutes with the shift, so the shift eigenvectors diagonalize all of them. This also explains why spectral graph methods become sensitive when the domain itself changes.

slides.title: Group Convolution Separates Domain From Symmetry
slides.notes: The important distinction is whether the symmetry group can be identified with the domain. On a cyclic grid it can, so outputs stay on the same index set. On the sphere, rotating filters produces a response over rotations, so later layers must know which space their signals inhabit.

slides.title: Manifolds Replace Global Shifts With Local Geometry
slides.notes: Make the limitation concrete: a general manifold does not let us slide a filter globally as though every point had a shared coordinate system. Instead, the metric supplies tangent spaces, exponential maps, and geodesics, which let us define local neighborhoods and intrinsic distances.

slides.title: Intrinsic Quantities Survive Deformation
slides.notes: This is the stability bridge between geometry and learning. If two shapes bend without stretching, geodesic distances and Laplace-Beltrami quantities remain meaningful. Direct eigenvectors may still be unstable, so practical filters are often expressed as functions of the operator rather than arbitrary spectral coefficients.

slides.title: Gauges Are Local Coordinate Choices
slides.notes: Students often identify a vector with its coordinate pair. Slow down here: the geometric vector is independent of a chosen tangent frame, while the numeric coordinates depend on that frame. Gauge symmetry asks the layer to ignore arbitrary frame choices while transforming features coherently.

slides.title: Gauge-Equivariant Filters Need Transport
slides.notes: The reason transport appears is simple but subtle: vectors at different points live in different fibers. Before a filter can compare them, it must move them to a common tangent space along a local path. The remaining filter must commute with the structure group representation.

slides.title: Meshes Sit Between Graphs And Manifolds
slides.notes: A triangular mesh is graph-like because it has vertices and edges, but the faces and edge lengths carry geometric information. The cotangent Laplacian is the teaching example: it is local and permutation-aware like a graph operator, while approximating an intrinsic manifold operator.

slides.title: Stable Mesh Filters Avoid Raw Eigenvectors
slides.notes: Connect the algebra back to computation. Polynomial filters apply repeated sparse Laplacian multiplications, so they are local and efficient. Rational filters trade compact support for resolution robustness. In both cases the filter is tied to the operator, not to fragile individual high-frequency eigenvectors.

slides.title: Functional Maps Reframe Remeshing
slides.notes: Permutation is only the simplest correspondence between two discretizations. Functional maps let us compare meshes with different vertices or connectivity by moving signals rather than matching point labels one by one. This is why spectra of intrinsic operators become remeshing-stable descriptors.

slides.title: The 5 Gs As A Design Checklist
slides.notes: Close by turning the taxonomy into a practical diagnostic. For any new model, ask what the domain is, what transformations should be invisible or equivariant, what locality means, and which arbitrary coordinates must be removed. The lab prompt is to deliberately break one assumption and watch the residual fail.
